A CONTINUAL CAPABILITY LAYER

Agent capabilities,
evolving independently.

A Harness Adapter contains only evolvable core: knowledge, prompts, code, roles, and capability declarations. The framework supplies the MCP wrapper and host integration. Evolve the core; reuse the infrastructure.

CONTEXT

A context document

Markdown introduces the adapter, its usage, and an optional briefing. The integration puts it into host context.

MCP TOOLS

A common tool interface

The framework turns declared core callables into MCP tools. No server implementation belongs inside an adapter.

AGENT DEFINITIONS

An optional role catalog

Roles need only a name, description, and instructions. After conversion, the Acting Harness loads them and manages instances.

    TWO STARTING ARCHITECTURES

    Choose the representation. Choose the Evolver separately.

    Prompt-only starts with an empty learned-context document. No adapter MCP server is registered. MWM starts with its knowledge structure and a single wm interface. Both produce candidates through the same framework.

    harnessadapter evolve --architecture prompt-only --learning-material ./learning-material --prompt "Improve ADAPTER.md."
harnessadapter evolve --architecture mwm --learning-material ./learning-material

    Prompt-oriented architecture does not imply a GEPA or SkillOpt implementation. Architecture guide ↗

    V0 / NATIVE SUBAGENT

    Define the role. Use host defaults.

    Roles are optional and need only three fields. Pass the concrete task when delegating; the Acting Harness creates and manages instances.

    model / tools / budget → host defaults
    name: researcher
description: Investigate project behavior and gather evidence
instructions: agents/researcher.md
    The current prototype reads adapter.json. Core functions and declarations are editable; the framework generates MCP launch settings and native role files outside the repo.
    PACKAGE

    A shareable package

    Code, prompts, interfaces, resource declarations, and optional initial knowledge. An architecture provides the starting point.

    INSTANCE

    A project instance

    Project settings, private LearningMaterial, runtime state, and resource bindings. Architecture updates do not overwrite learned content.

    REVISION

    A consistent revision

    Identifies compatible code and knowledge state. External state declares snapshot, migration, or reconstruction behavior.

    ↳

    Training State is optional. Stateful Evolvers return it separately from the Adapter; stateless Evolvers return none. Acting agents consume the Adapter, not the training state.

    IMPLEMENTED / MWM REFERENCE
    Original MWM structure, framework-owned delivery.
    The MWM Evolver runs through Codex or Claude Code using framework-enforced capabilities. It can revise every core file. The framework retains LearningMaterial, execution logs, and candidate status outside the repo. The original source is never activated or overwritten automatically.
    harnessadapter evolve mwm --learning-material examples/mwm_evidence
    The initial simplified demo was not a faithful MWM port. The corrected learner used the original contract, skills, and patterns, producing six knowledge/journal/case artifacts through one wm interface. It kept unresolved assumptions open and created no speculative executable. Read the correction and verification ↗ · Read the deployment bridge ↗

    A
    Optional helpers, explicit readiness
    Native mechanisms, manual configuration, or external frameworks can handle integration. Even with our helpers, generated files do not prove successful loading.
    B
    Fixed definitions, on-demand instances
    v0 loads roles before formal tasks. New definitions enter the next run without relying on hot loading. Performance improvements require separate evaluation.
    
  
    

  
    
    
    05 / TWO WAYS IN
    One SDK. Two orchestrators.
    The CLI supplies a default deployment and evolution flow. 
    External frameworks reuse the SDK and retain orchestration.
    
    
    FOR ADAPTER USERS
      The repository-local CLI works for Codex and Claude Code. A public SDK and Reef bridge remain design goals.
      terminal · proposed CLI
      
    
      INTEGRATION RULE
      One update chain, one release authority. The default Manager owns standalone release decisions; Reef owns them when embedded. Candidate experiments cannot silently change the running instance.
      
  
      

  
      
    
      06 / SCOPE & NEXT STEPS
      Prove reuse. Then grow the ecosystem.
      MWM provides a starting implementation. 
      Different implementations must test the shared framework.
      
    
      Phase 1 · Design goal
      A complete working loop
      • Implement Markdown, MCP, and optional role exports
      • Support direct integration and optional preparation/checks
      • Integrate an external evolver with different internals
      • Cover a simple skill and stateful tools
      Phase 2 · Test boundaries
      Across hosts and orchestrators
      • Run the same adapter on two hosts
      • Let Reef call the same evolution capability
      • Bind an independent model, such as a 4B search helper
      • Measure integration effort and actual utility
      Later · After adoption
      Sharing and shared maintenance
      • Independent third-party adapters and evolvers
      • Clear compatibility and capability declarations
      • Architecture publication and revision distribution
      • Build a marketplace around real demand
      
    
      STILL OPEN
      Questions for implementation
      What counts as supporting a host?+
      v0 must verify Context, MCP tools, and optional native roles before formal tasks. Returning host records requires a separate integration; hot loading is not a baseline requirement.
      How do we migrate and restore persistent state?+
      Code and state revisions jointly define a loadable instance. Indexes can declare reconstruction; databases need snapshots or migrations. Git rollback cannot undo irreversible external actions.
      Are all evolvers interchangeable?+
      No. Each evolver should declare the adapter types it understands, required feedback, and editable scope. The framework checks compatibility while preserving internal search and update processes.
      Which parts of MWM belong in the common protocol?+
      Revision, resource, invocation, and update boundaries fit common contracts. Public consumption uses Context, MCP Tools, and optional Agent Definitions. Memory directories, claim representations, briefing, journal, and learning agenda remain MWM internals.
      
    
      Success criterion
      Another author can complete the loop with their own method,
      without understanding or adopting MWM internals.

      2026.09.18 / DISCUSSION 001Design agreed · Implementation ahead
      Repos, three exports, and pre-task integration
      Define the basic adapter unit and initial consumption boundaries across Acting Harness, Harness Adapter, and Meta Harness.
      
      
      01 / BASIC UNIT
      An adapter is an independent repo. MWM is a reference; knowledge structures remain open.
      02 / THREE EXPORTS
      Markdown Context, optional MCP Tools, and optional Agent Definitions.
      03 / EXECUTION OWNERSHIP
      The Acting Harness launches and manages subagents. A 4B search helper is a tool.
      04 / MINIMAL DEFINITION
      Roles require only name, description, and instructions. Other runtime settings use effective host defaults.
      05 / LOADING TIME
      Verify readiness before tasks. Definitions stay fixed for the run; instances start on demand. Bootstrap / Connector is optional.
      06 / PRODUCT MODES
      A public SDK and standalone CLI share facilities. External frameworks can retain update orchestration.
      
      
      Why expand text plus MCP into three interfaces?+
      MCP tools do not themselves register native host agents. Separate role definitions clarify responsibility for conversion, loading, and execution.
      
      
      Why not standardize every subagent parameter now?+
      The survey keeps about 20 common fields as extension candidates. v0 reduces the meta-agent's configuration burden with simple roles; models, tools, and budgets use effective host defaults.
      
      
      Why require roles to be ready before formal tasks?+
      Host hot-loading behavior varies. Preparation and loading happen before tasks, through the host, user, or external framework. Our Bootstrap / Connector is only an optional helper.
      
      
      Next discussion
      The later core-only design is implemented as a Python prototype. Next: dependency/resource brokers, stronger execution isolation, external Evolvers, and state migration.
